items.title: Spain and Argentina Clash in Historic World Cup Final
items.body: Spain and Argentina meet in the World Cup final on Sunday, pitting the European and South American champions against each other for the first time. The historic clash has sparked debate over continental football supremacy. Millions across Spain will tune in, with public screenings set up in major cities. Residents can expect a festive atmosphere and possible schedule disruptions.

items.title: Average Down Payment Tops €170,000 in Spain's Priciest Cities
items.body: Buying a 90-square-meter home in San Sebastián now requires savings of €178,487, while in Madrid the figure stands at €172,987. Palma, Barcelona, Málaga, and Bilbao also demand over €100,000 upfront. No Spanish capital offers a purchase with just €30,000 in savings, a new report shows. The soaring entry costs shut out many would-be buyers, particularly younger households and foreign residents without substantial capital.

items.title: CJEU Validates Spain's Amnesty Law for Catalonia
items.body: The Grand Chamber of the Court of Justice of the EU ruled that Spain's Amnesty Law for Catalonia does not violate EU law or the Union's financial interests. The decision upholds the legality of a law that grants pardons to Catalan separatists involved in the 2017 independence push. The ruling removes a major legal hurdle and could ease political tensions in Spain.

items.title: 34 Arrested in Fake Domestic Partnership Residency Scheme
items.body: Police dismantled two networks that charged €10,000 to €12,000 to arrange fraudulent domestic partnerships for residency permits. The scheme mainly targeted Moroccan citizens and involved falsifying notarial acts, rental contracts, and empadronamiento (municipal registration) documents. Officers arrested 34 people, are investigating 62 others, and have issued 21 arrest warrants. Foreign residents are urged to avoid such illegal services as enforcement intensifies.

items.title: Food Prices Could Jump Up to 9% in 2027
items.body: Economists predict food inflation across Europe will reach 5–9% in 2027, driven by the war in Iran and intensifying heatwaves. Heatwaves alone could add up to 1 percentage point to annual inflation, while rising production costs contribute another 0.5–0.7 points. The forecast signals higher grocery bills for Spanish households, adding to the cost-of-living squeeze.

items.title: Gasoline Prices Rise Again as VAT Discount Ends
items.body: Gasoline and diesel prices have increased for a second straight week following the return of full 21% VAT. A litre of gasoline now costs €1.541 on average, up 1.58%, while diesel sits at €1.549, a 0.91% rise. A new government discount of 15 cents per litre in July, sliding to 10 cents in August and 5 cents in September, aims to cushion the impact. Commuters and drivers across Spain will feel the pinch at the pump.

items.title: Irregular Migration to Spain Drops 25%, but Ceuta Arrivals Surge
items.body: Spain recorded 14,479 irregular arrivals by mid-July 2026, a 24.7% drop from 19,222 a year earlier. However, land crossings into the enclave of Ceuta jumped 149%, underscoring ongoing border pressure. The shifting patterns may influence government migration policy, while communities along the coast and border remain on alert.

items.title: Electoral Board Clarifies Voting Rules for New 'Grandchildren Law' Citizens
items.body: The Junta Electoral Central (JEC) has ordered that newly naturalized citizens under the 'grandchildren law' must justify their electoral municipality if it differs from their last residence in Spain. The law grants nationality to descendants of Spanish exiles, and officials want to prevent improper voter registration. The ruling is expected to affect thousands of new voters ahead of future elections.

items.title: EU Report Criticizes Spanish Government for Pressuring Judges
items.body: The European Commission's Rule of Law report criticized the Spanish government for publicly pressuring judges. It cited the conviction of former prosecutor general García Ortiz and officials' dismissal of another ruling as 'judicial masonry.' The rebuke underscores persistent institutional friction that may worry residents concerned about the country's legal stability.

items.title: African Air Mass Could Trigger Third Heatwave of Summer
items.body: A surge of hot air from North Africa is set to push temperatures up from Saturday, potentially creating the summer's third official heatwave. Highs of 35°C are expected across much of the country, with southeastern areas and the Guadalquivir valley reaching 40°C. Health authorities advise residents to stay hydrated, avoid outdoor activity during peak hours, and check on vulnerable neighbours.

items.title: Lidl Spain Agrees to 15% Pay Raise and €280M Investment
items.body: Lidl and Spanish unions sealed a labour deal that will lift salaries by a cumulative 15% through 2030, with a 4% hike in 2026 and 3% annually from 2027 to 2029. The supermarket chain also pledged to invest over €280 million in the next four years and improve working conditions and hours. The agreement may set a benchmark for pay negotiations across the retail sector.

items.title: Court Overturns €25M Fine Against Iberdrola for Market Manipulation
items.body: The Audiencia Nacional annulled the €25 million penalty that the competition watchdog CNMC had imposed on Iberdrola for allegedly manipulating electricity prices in 2013. The move follows a criminal court's acquittal of the energy giant on the same facts. The ruling limits regulators' ability to punish past market conduct and could influence future energy oversight.

items.title: Zaragoza Wildfire Burns 7,600 Hectares, 60-Km Perimeter
items.body: A forest fire in Orés, Zaragoza, has burned 7,600 hectares and carved a 60-kilometer perimeter, becoming one of the region's most complex blazes in years. Emergency crews are working to contain the flames, though no major evacuations have been reported so far. Residents in nearby areas should monitor air quality and stay informed of local alerts.
